intro: AI tools for paralegals on Mac help most with the work you already do in Word, Outlook and Gmail. Lazur is a voice assistant: you hold a key, ask, and it answers out loud, points at what you need on screen, and drafts text for you to check. It does not click for you or change your files.
tldr: Paralegal work is mostly documents, research, drafting, email and filing, according to the BLS list of duties.
No public study I could open measures how a paralegal's day splits by task. Track your own week to find out.
Lazur explains, points, guides, dictates, drafts, researches and sets reminders. It does not click buttons or edit files.
Follow your employer's rules on client data before a real file or screenshot goes near any AI tool.
Microsoft gave October 2026 as the end date for legacy Outlook for Mac. That date has passed, so check which version you run.

blocks.text: What a paralegal's day involves on a computer

Paralegal work runs on documents, research and email. The Bureau of Labor Statistics lists the core duties. You investigate and gather case facts. You research laws and regulations. You gather, organize and maintain legal documents. You draft correspondence and legal documents such as contracts. You obtain affidavits, handle exhibits at trial, and file exhibits, briefs and appeals. You schedule interviews and depositions. Several of those duties happen in Word and Outlook on your Mac, so that is where an AI tool can help first.
Where a paralegal's time goes: what the research shows

Nobody has measured how a paralegal's day splits across tasks, at least not in any source I could open for this page. The BLS list describes the job. It does not time it. If you read a percentage that says most of the day goes to email, ask where it came from. Your own week will tell you more than a number for an entire profession.

The closest number is a forecast. Thomson Reuters' 2024 Future of Professionals report surveyed more than 2,200 professionals across legal, tax, and risk and compliance. Respondents predicted AI would free up four hours a week in the next year, and 12 hours a week within five years. That prediction covers all three fields combined. It is not a count of paralegal admin time, and it does not say how the four hours would be spent.
Which task goes to which Lazur mode

Lazur's modes are explain, point, guide, dictate, draft, research and everyday tasks. Each mode does a different job. Explaining and pointing keep you in control of the app. Drafting and dictation produce text that you check. Research runs in the background and comes back with a report. None of the modes clicks a button for you.

blocks.text: Worked example: preparing a deposition notice in Word

Say you need a notice of deposition for a witness on Thursday. You already have a Word template from the last case. Open it and hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask where the caption block sits. Lazur circles the caption area and labels it, so you can find the lines to change without scrolling the whole file. Type the party names yourself. A wrong name is easy to miss on a second read.

Next, hold fn and dictate the date, the time, the location and the court reporter's name. Dictation puts clean text at the cursor. Then ask Lazur to draft a short cover email to opposing counsel, and paste it into a new message in Outlook. Read the email once for tone and once for facts. Check the deposition time against your calendar before you send anything.
Drafting correspondence without starting from a blank page

Drafting is where a voice assistant saves the most typing. Give Lazur the facts in plain sentences. Tell it who will read the letter, what you need from them, and how firm the tone should be. Lazur types the first draft at your cursor. You then compare each date, amount and section number with the file before anything leaves your Mac.

Keep the source on screen. Lazur works from what is in front of it and from what you say. If a letter quotes an agreement, open that agreement first and ask Lazur to draft the quote. The most common mistake is trusting the first pass. A draft can sound right and still cite the wrong paragraph. Read it as if you were the opposing lawyer looking for an error.
Research: what an AI assistant can and cannot do for you

Lazur research jobs run in Lazur's own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension. The job comes back with a summary and a report. Use that to get oriented. Find out which rule applies, where the court posts its forms, or where a statute is printed. Then open the primary source yourself and read the exact wording before you rely on it.

blocks.title: Verify before you cite
blocks.text: A research summary is a starting point, not a citation. Open the official rule, statute or order, read the exact text, and check when the source was last updated.

Worked example: you need the filing deadline for a motion to compel in your county. Ask Lazur for a research job that names the court. Open each link in the report and find the rule that sets the deadline. Confirm whether the court counts calendar days or court days. Then add the deadline to Calendar yourself, with a reminder a few days earlier.

Watch for one common mistake. A summary can merge two rules from two different courts. Check the court name in each source. If the report mixes them, ask again with a narrower question about one court only.
Email in Outlook and Gmail: Reply All and the wrong attachment

Email is where paralegals make the expensive mistakes. Microsoft's Outlook for Mac page lists Mail Tips, which warn you about large Reply All lists and sensitive data. New Outlook for Mac also has a customizable toolbar, Microsoft Search, My Day for a daily calendar agenda, Snooze, and nested compose in the Reading Pane. Those features help with the follow-up work that fills a paralegal's inbox.

Check which Outlook you run. Microsoft calls the current app new Outlook for Mac, and the older app legacy Outlook for Mac. Microsoft's page names the switch New Outlook and Legacy Outlook. It says you can go back with Help > Revert to Legacy Outlook. Microsoft said legacy support would end in October 2026. SMU IT gave October 1, 2026 as the stop date, and that date has passed. If you still use legacy, ask your IT team what to do before you update anything.

blocks.title: Legacy Outlook support
blocks.text: Microsoft's stated end date, October 2026, has already passed. Going back to legacy may no longer work, and support depends on your Microsoft 365, Office or Outlook license.

Run a recipient check every time. Before you press Send, count the people in the To and Cc lines. Look for an exhibit with a privilege stamp or a client's personal details. Mail Tips may warn you, but it will not stop you. Lazur can explain a warning on screen and dictate a clean reply, but it does not press Send.

In Gmail, Lazur can help you write replies by voice. Hold fn, speak the reply, and check the recipients before you send. For a longer look at the email side of the job, read [Outlook for paralegals on Mac](/for/paralegals/outlook).
Word: finding terms and moving through long files

Word for Mac has a few shortcuts that pay off every day. Microsoft's keyboard shortcuts page lists ⌘F for Find, which moves focus to the Search in Document box. It lists ⌘Z for Undo, and F1 also works for Undo. It lists ⌘C to copy and ⌘V to paste. Some Mac shortcuts conflict with macOS defaults, and Microsoft marks those with an asterisk. None of the five it lists carries the mark.

Defined terms cause the most trouble. A lease may call a party Lessee on page one and Tenant later on. Search for both. If you lose the Search in Document box, ask Lazur where it is. Then press ⌘F and type the term. Read each hit, because a search finds the word, not the meaning.
Client data: check the rules before anything goes to an AI tool

Follow your employer's rules on client data. Your firm, your court and your clients may limit which tools you can use and what can leave the office. This guide cannot tell you what your firm allows. Ask your supervising attorney or IT team before you test any tool with a real file.

Here is what Lazur does with what it sees. It listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer your question, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Lazur makes no compliance claim for your firm. The rules for your files still come from your employer.

blocks.title: Close what you do not need
blocks.text: A screenshot shows everything on screen, not only the line you care about. Close other clients' files and emails before you hold the shortcut.
Ask about the clause, not the client. You can often say explain this indemnity clause and let the clause on screen do the work. Keep names out of your questions when the clause alone answers them.
Mistakes paralegals make with AI tools

items: Trusting a summary without opening the source document or the official rule.
Asking for a draft before the facts are on screen, so the draft fills the gaps with guesses.
Sending a Reply All to a long list because the first name looked right.
Dictating a client or witness name and not checking the spelling against the file.
Assuming a shortcut or menu works the same after an app update. Check the screen first.

blocks.text: How to start this week

items: Pick one task from the table that you do every day, such as a cover email.
Check your employer's rules on AI tools and client data before you test anything with a real file.
Get Lazur from the [download page](/download) and start the trial, which needs no credit card.
Ask Lazur to explain one screen you use often, then check the answer in the app.
Note each mistake for a month, then change one habit at a time.

blocks.text: Pricing and where to go next

Plans and AI action limits are on the [pricing page](/pricing). Dictation is unlimited on both paid plans, so a long string of file notes does not add to your bill. For Word steps, read [Word for paralegals on Mac](/for/paralegals/word) and [AI assistant for Word on Mac](/apps/word).
If you change only one habit, make it the recipient check. It takes seconds and prevents the most embarrassing mistakes in the job.

faq.question: Are AI tools for paralegals allowed at my firm?
faq.answer: That depends on your firm, your court and your client agreements. Follow your employer's rules on client data before you use any AI tool with a real file. This page does not make a compliance claim for Lazur or for your firm, and it cannot tell you what your firm allows.

faq.question: Where does a paralegal's time actually go?
faq.answer: No public study I could open measures that split. The Bureau of Labor Statistics lists the duties, including gathering facts, researching, organizing documents, drafting, filing and scheduling. Track your own week for a few days to see where your time goes.

faq.question: Can Lazur file documents or send email for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It points at things, explains them, guides you one click at a time, drafts text and types it. You file the document and press Send yourself.

faq.question: Does Lazur run on Windows?
faq.answer: No. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned but not available. You can start from the [download page](/download).

faq.question: Which Outlook should I use on my Mac?
faq.answer: Microsoft calls the current app new Outlook for Mac. It calls the older app legacy Outlook for Mac. Microsoft said legacy support would end in October 2026, and that date has passed. Check with your IT team before you change versions.

faq.question: Are Word shortcuts the same on a Mac?
faq.answer: Microsoft lists ⌘Z for undo, ⌘C to copy, ⌘V to paste and ⌘F to find in Word for Mac. Some Mac shortcuts conflict with macOS defaults, and Microsoft marks those with an asterisk. Check the full list on Microsoft's page before you rely on one.

faq.question: What happens to a screenshot Lazur takes?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer your question. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models.

faq.question: Can I cite what Lazur finds in research?
faq.answer: Not directly. A research report is a starting point. Open the official rule, statute or court order, read the exact wording, and check the date. Then cite the source you read yourself.

faq.question: How much does Lazur cost?
faq.answer: Plans, prices and AI action limits are on the [pricing page](/pricing). Dictation is unlimited on the paid plans.

painPoints.title: Documents spread everywhere
painPoints.text: BLS lists gathering, organizing and maintaining legal documents as a core duty. The files sit in email attachments, Word folders and shared drives, so finding the right version takes longer than it should.

painPoints.title: Email that can go wrong fast
painPoints.text: One Reply All can send a sensitive exhibit to people who should not see it. Outlook for Mac shows Mail Tips warnings, but you still have to read them before you press Send.

painPoints.title: Drafting from a blank page
painPoints.text: Letters, contracts and requests for affidavits start from nothing unless you have a template. BLS names drafting correspondence and legal documents as part of the job.

painPoints.title: Research that still needs checking
painPoints.text: Looking up a rule means several browser tabs, a PDF and a second search. The answer still needs a check against the official text before you use it.

painPoints.title: Deadlines kept in three places
painPoints.text: Deadlines end up in Calendar, in email threads and in a paper note on the desk. A missed deadline is the error nobody wants to explain to a supervising attorney.
